To identify the effect of Scenario 1 on the area's growth, the baseline situation needs to be examined. Although somewhat lower, the growth projected for the baseline, closely parallels the growth pattern just discussed. Scenario 1 is responsible for half of the total rapid growth in 1979. If other coal development is delayed, this increase would be significantly smaller. Between 1979 and 1986 there would be about 1100 more people in the impact area if moderate coal development occurs, compared with the baseline situation. The decrease in 1986-1989 is entirely caused by Scenario 1 activities, and thereafter Scenario 1 accounts for approximately 300-400 additional people.
Community Population - All new impact area residents are projected to locate in the existing communities of the Big Horn and Little Big Horn valleys. Growth was allocated to the communities by race in proportion to present community make-up. In addition, only Non-Crow migration is expected to occur in Hardin.
Wyola, Lodge Grass and Crow Agency are predominantly Indian at this time. Because of the allocation scheme described above, these three communities will grow at a fairly rapid, steady rate whether or not coal development takes place, becoming increasingly Indian dominated. These communities will remain largely unaffected by the low level development proposed by Westmoreland. The growth rates in Lodge Grass are similar to Crow Agency's; they were not graphed separately in Figure III-6.
